# Exposure audit of the twelve proposed holdouts

**All twelve have prior design exposure in existing repository records. None can be presented as untouched on the evidence inspected here.** This is a conservative exposure assessment, not an evaluation manifest, a certification of contamination completeness, or a selection of replacement cases. No external sources or new prospective cases were retrieved.

The approved migration design says cases already used to design the kernel are development challenges, not untouched holdouts (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-semantic-kernel-design.md:56–59`). The twelve-name table in the adopted source plan is not just a list: its rows describe mechanisms, the following paragraphs analyze them, and line394 explicitly uses the group to favor a kernel based on state, effects, interfaces, authority, timing and assumptions. Several cases are then used again to specify concrete future financial libraries. That design use predates the later implemented kernel freezes.

The cited source-plan lines are retained from commit `43c2b1b264f542d3ef741130373115ed1b62b5a6`, committed September6,2026 at14:07:26−06:00, before the first transition-pilot commit. Older original corpus examples are retained from `93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676`, committed August4,2026 at09:05:40−06:00. These are repository-history dates, not verified original research/publication dates. Exact line-introduction commits, source-file hashes, Git blobs and line hashes are in `assessment.json`.

## Case assessment

In this table, **plan** means `docs/research/2026-09-06-defi-source-plan.md`; **original corpus documents** means the supplied `corpus/elementsdefi.md` and `corpus/elementsdefiGPT.md`, which are broader than the separate normalized72-row dataset. Each case has the same conservative eligibility: **development-exposed; do not label untouched**.

| Proposed case | Meaningful existing design use beyond its proposal-table row | Prior corpus/model context and identity boundary |
|---|---|---|
| dYdX Chain | Plan373/388 uses node-local books and price-time matching to motivate ordering/finality. | Original corpus explicitly decomposes dYdX v4 as an app-chain order book: `elementsdefi.md:225,239`; `elementsdefiGPT.md:198,424`. Chain/v4 is a conceptual alias supported by those descriptions; no deployment pin is inferred. v3 is separate family context. |
| Osmosis | Plan374/388 analyzes heterogeneous pool/order-book routing. | Original corpus uses Osmosis for concentrated liquidity, TWAP and execution-model independence: `elementsdefiGPT.md:128,196,232,474`. No version/deployment is fixed. |
| DeepBookV3 | Plan375/388 analyzes Pool/state/book/vault/balance-manager objects to separate matching and accounting; line394 incorporates the cases into kernel design. | No additional named corpus/model use was found in the bounded search. That absence does not erase the substantive plan exposure or certify untouched source. |
| THORChain | Plan376/388/912 uses native cross-chain swaps to motivate asynchronous message lifecycle/finality assumptions and reject atomic same-state wiring as a general model. | No additional standalone local protocol model was identified. Exact name and architectural use are already present. |
| Velocity | Plan377/390/916–920 uses shared margin/lendable collateral, unsettled profit and loss socialization to motivate claims, liabilities and a margin/funding library. | Other “velocity” matches concern visualization motion and are excluded. No resolved deployment identity is claimed. |
| Kamino | Plan378/390 analyzes allocation weights/caps, LTVs, rate curves and oracles. | Listed in original corpus (`elementsdefi.md:72,284`); earlier Steakhouse research and its specification discuss Kamino as an allocation substrate (`expansion/12-prediction/01-research.md:745–746,906–908`; `specs/steakhouse-financial.json:31`). This is nested-product exposure, not a standalone normalized Kamino row. |
| Euler V2 | Plan379/390 describes modular credit vaults, EVC batching, subaccounts, operators and controller authority. | Explicit Euler v2 isolated-market example in `elementsdefiGPT.md:210`. Unversioned Euler appears inside two Steakhouse rows. The actual historical atlas names **Euler v1** (`formal/atlas.qnt:189`), which is not evidence of V2 deployment use. Retained Steakhouse research disputes the broad Euler substrate attribution; this audit does not resolve it. |
| Term Finance | Plan380/390 analyzes recurring fixed-term auctions and rate discovery. | Already a named fixed-term-debt library example E017 in `elementsdefiGPT.md:213`. No standalone normalized72 row or deployment pin is inferred. |
| UMA Optimistic Oracle | Plan323/381 uses UMA to distinguish truth/dispute dependencies from economic-function categories. | Original taxonomy E030 (`elementsdefiGPT.md:233`), Across and Polymarket rows, bundled prediction-market comparisons, and actual Quint model text already discuss optimistic resolution (`corpus50/lanes/lane2…json:383`; `lane3…json:349,408`; `quint-models/L6/common.qnt:146`; `quint-models-v2/polymarket.qnt:82`). Dependency exposure is not standalone UMA protocol coverage or a verified source correspondence. |
| Nexus Mutual | Plan382/392/924–926 specifies a conditional cover claim whose discharge relies on externally adjudicated proof of loss. | Original mutual-cover example E026 (`elementsdefiGPT.md:222`) and an old solver's vocabulary-support counterexample (`algebra/solvers/OP-LOG/theory.py:317–322`, `algebra/reports/OP-LOG.md:525–527`). zkLink “Nexus” is unrelated and excluded. |
| Lightning Network | Plan383/392/912 uses chained conditional payments to motivate obligations, timeouts, asynchronous settlement and cross-domain assumptions. | No further standalone local protocol encoding was identified. Lightning shorthand in those paragraphs is tied to the explicit candidate name; no complete alias search or deployment mapping is claimed. |
| Balancer V3 | Plan384/392/880–886 prescribes shared Vault accounting, transient deltas and settlement postconditions;1105 selects the mechanism for porting. | Original corpus includes Balancer v2 and pool-family examples; corpus50 category residue explicitly mentions V3 (`lane1…json:92`). Sprint8's design investigation explicitly cites the source-plan shared/transient sections (`wiki-llm/sprint-8-atomic-synchronization-draft.md:37–40`). Its implemented loan/return model expressly leaves full Balancer fidelity open (`:180–185`). This is strong design exposure, not a V2=V3 alias or deployed equivalence claim. |

## Corpus membership and repeated evidence

None of these twelve names/family patterns matches a standalone `original.name` among the72 normalized source records or `identity.label` among the75 normalization candidates. **That does not establish novelty.** The older supplied corpus documents, nested component references, category residue, library examples and actual historical model text are distinct evidence surfaces. UMA appears inside Across/Polymarket and a bundled prediction-market comparison; unversioned Euler appears inside Steakhouse; Kamino appears in prior research/specification of that substrate; Balancer V3 appears in category-level residue despite exclusion from the top-five rows.

Search results include copies in review bundles and graph outputs; those copies are not independent design events. The raw lexical inventory also deliberately retains false-positive candidates for inspection. Excluded examples include constant-velocity UI motion, the academic `maude.lcc.uma.es` domain, zkLink Nexus, generic load balancers and Euler v1 when reasoning specifically about V2. Existing citation tokens/URLs are provenance text, not newly verified financial sources.

## Scope, preservation and artifacts

The deterministic search covered20,047 existing tracked UTF-8 text files selected by `git ls-files`, excluding dependency/build/vendor directories and this new output directory. Symlinks were not followed. `all-name-matches.jsonl` preserves every discovered matched line's path, line, columns, context and hash; `scan-inputs.json` records scope, patterns and every scanned file's byte hash. The graphify source graph was checked for scope orientation, but it excludes research/corpus documentation and cannot certify exposure absence.

`assessment.json` contains12 case judgments and47 selected source-evidence records, including retained path histories and exact line-level Git provenance. History checking follows selected extant paths and their blamed lines; it does not exhaust deleted/unreachable/private records, untracked files, unmentioned aliases or prior human knowledge. No case is certified untouched, no replacement was read or selected, and no evaluation manifest or implementation was edited.

All88 frozen Sprint10 inputs and every selected historical evidence source remained byte-identical. Of338 checked existing input/context files, four active corpus-planning files changed concurrently after the scan: the corpus-adjudication design, dispute inventory, evidence-adjudication specification and corpus planning draft. Root confirmed these were its authorized CP01 correction after the financial batch release; originals and the correction record are retained under `review/semantic-kernel/corpus-provenance-adjudication/planning/root-findings/`. This audit did not edit them; their exact before/current hashes are recorded as planning-context drift, so the report does not falsely claim all scanned context remained stable. Those changing files supply no selected evidence for the twelve-case conclusions.

The two scripts reconstruct discovery and the explicit assessment from existing files and refuse to overwrite their principal inventories. A future rerun should use a fresh output revision and bind its own repository state; reproducing current working-tree bytes is not assumed. `verification.json` and `artifact-inventory.json` record the final integrity checks and artifact hashes. This work changes only the new audit directory.

Where documentation and implementation diverge (e.g., Aave docs describing \"stable rate\" borrowing that was later disabled in practice; MakerDAO \"CDP\" docs vs \"Vault\" implementation naming), I note the divergence in the attribute table.","line_sha256":"5b9a5a96f6908028c012b05f5fbd263e9503752cc21e2f96cc06e677c4891bc1","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"},{"line":284,"text":"- **Non-EVM coverage is adequate but not exhaustive:** Solana (Save, Kamino, MarginFi, Drift, Meteora, Raydium/Orca), Cosmos (dYdX v4, Osmosis), and Move/Cardano-eUTxO are represented enough to confirm elements are largely execution-model-independent, but Bitcoin-L2 and Cardano DeFi are thin in the corpus and could hide execution-model-specific elements.","line_sha256":"52283e705c170f446348af2b36233f9fbbc3d5412a3929012be2d08056f6304f","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"}]},"corpus/elementsdefiGPT.md:128,196,232,474":{"path":"corpus/elementsdefiGPT.md","sha256":"3ae40c440bfee5ccd89a2e6e2434163f9cfa1dc31468a24fc30e6d5ef8389798","git_blob":"cd950e64518ef3179db6b28c75fc612e890bbf03","lines":[{"line":128,"text":"The non-EVM subset includes Orca, Raydium, OpenBook, Drift, Mango and Solend on Solana; Osmosis, Mars and Kujira in Cosmos environments; Cetus, NAVI and Thala in Move environments; Minswap, Liqwid and Indigo on Cardano; and Sovryn and ALEX in Bitcoin-linked environments. Their documentation demonstrates that concentrated liquidity, lending, collateralized synthetic assets, order books, and liquidation queues can be implemented under account-based, object-based, app-chain, and eUTxO execution models. This supports treating those mechanisms as execution-model-independent, while atomicity, sequencing, and interface details remain reaction conditions. citeturn12search25turn12search2turn12search15turn12search28turn12search22turn12search33","line_sha256":"bfc996cc4aa17b297452e392c7373d00537a9cae7e74156f113d52ea435956ac","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"},{"line":196,"text":"| E007 | **Cl — concentrated liquidity** | Pool pricing / P1 | Uniswap v3; Orca Whirlpools; Cetus; Osmosis CL | Tick/range state, position claims, active-liquidity accounting | Tick spacing, range, fee tier | Range exhaustion, JIT/adverse selection, tick bugs; mature |","line_sha256":"89c1d60cd51a0261bb1609d609a3c145b80ae96fe042ddd66d5a07b8aa000777","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"},{"line":232,"text":"| E029 | **Tp — on-chain time-weighted price** | Truth / P2 | Uniswap v2/v3; Osmosis TWAP | Sufficient market depth and observations over time | Window, observation cardinality | Multi-block manipulation, stale observation, liquidity migration; mature |","line_sha256":"6b1ea851cf74a7d9c919c85fbd52b0864c91455bee702801b54a01f3b0a81544","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"},{"line":474,"text":"The table says these systems are molecularly equivalent at the financial-mechanism level. Practitioners may still distinguish them by account/object ownership, transaction scheduling, keeper requirements, incentive programs, token semantics and user interfaces. Those differences are isotopes, environmental conditions or residue unless they create a new recurring state transition and failure signature. Osmosis and Cetus documentation confirms that concentrated-liquidity semantics can recur across Cosmos and Move environments even though implementation and state-access models differ. Conversely, \"vault\" names five different things across Yearn (strategy mixture), MakerDAO (CDP), ERC-4626 (share interface), Balancer (singleton custody), and Uniswap v4 (singleton PoolManager) — these are NOT one element.","line_sha256":"d8b8342299f33ce0dd015a3d6936cc8748e327b0edf50f75410192ff4f9bcac2","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"},{"line":216,"text":"7. **Balancer** = `AMM[weighted-geomean]{weights} · singleton-custody` — n-token isotope.","line_sha256":"0d4eddc1a8b49e4c7b7300a83ba434bb125ebce729b6092465167da31f2fe649","retained_line_commit":"93ee29dacf2963e6957b16220f31412dda329676","committer_epoch":"1785855940","committer_timezone":"-0600"}]},"corpus/elementsdefiGPT.md:27,194,416":{"path":"corpus/elementsdefiGPT.md","sha256":"3ae40c440bfee5ccd89a2e6e2434163f9cfa1dc31468a24fc30e6d5ef8389798","git_blob":"cd950e64518ef3179db6b28c75fc612e890bbf03","lines":[{"line":27,"text":"A **true compound** has a shared state machine, balance sheet, settlement rule, or solvency invariant. A **mixture** merely routes among components that remain independently redeemable and independently insolvent. An aggregator such as 1inch is therefore normally a mixture; a Balancer Vault plus a weighted pool is a compound because custody, accounting, and settlement are jointly coordinated. # Concrete-instance correspondence audit

**The fresh bounded checks pass; concrete all-input correspondence remains unestablished.** All five root observations are confirmed, with the distinction that the composition equation remains a meaningful bounded check even though the identification of `ex` with `maxOf` is built into the script.

The unchanged `formal/v3/m5-convex.mjs` ran at `4d42600082d4213d34ac5ab4b0dfc3eefde23d5e` under Node **v24.18.1**, completed in **14.83 seconds**, and produced empty stderr. [Execution identity](execution.json) records exact UTC times, command, environment, source revision and raw log hashes. [Raw stdout](stdout.log) contains the actual counts. This audit checked every expected result block and its nonempty denominator; exit zero alone was not treated as success.

| Actual current result | LSTAR | PARSED_NEW |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Extracted edge occurrences / distinct edges | 13 / 12 | 16 / 15 |
| Vertices / SCCs / nontrivial SCCs | 58 / 58 / 0 | 58 / 58 / 0 |
| Nonempty size 1–3 equality seeds / mismatches | 32,567 / 0 | 32,567 / 0 |
| Fixed singleton/pair union splits / failures | 30,856 / 0 | 30,856 / 0 |
| Distinct closed states in anti-exchange loop | 1,700 | 1,697 |
| Ordered outside-point tests / violations | 5,169,336 / 0 | 5,142,758 / 0 |
| Generator-index composition pairs / failures | 1,464,616 / 0 | 1,464,616 / 0 |
| Singleton closures equal to their seed | 49 / 58 | 48 / 58 |

## What the execution establishes

At `m5:49–60`, both `Cn` and `reach` are defined locally from the same extracted adjacency. They use different traversal algorithms, so disagreement can expose an implementation error. Their agreement does **not** compare a separately shipped closure implementation to graph reachability. No closure export from `lib.mjs` or another implementation is called.

At `m5:93–102`, `ex(A)` is defined as `maxOf(A)`. The experiment therefore does not test the intrinsic definition `a ∉ Cn(A \ {a})` against maximal elements. It does test the resulting composition identity on its selected states. Calling the entire test a tautology would overcorrect the evidence.

The equality loop omits the empty set: its exact denominator is `58 + choose(58,2) + choose(58,3) = 32,567`. Including empty would yield 32,568. The union loop tests only `A={E[i]}`, `B={E[j],E[k]}` for `i<j<k`; it does not test every partition or every pair of small sets.

Anti-exchange deduplicates closures of singleton/pair generators and explicitly adds empty. Its point loop uses ordered, distinct `x,y` outside each closed state, rather than every `58²` pair. It covers only that selected closed-state family.

Composition has **1,711 generator indices**, formed with `i≤j`, and does not deduplicate their closures. The distinct nonempty state counts are therefore 1,699 and 1,696, derived from the anti-exchange state counts minus empty. There are respectively 12 and 15 redundant index entries. The reported 1,464,616 pairs are index pairs with repetition; the corresponding distinct unordered state-pair counts are 1,444,150 and 1,439,056. Empty is absent from this loop.

All violation counters only print. None sets a failing exit code or throws. This wrapper's parsed-counter verdict is separate from the historical script's process status.

An additional scope guard: `definiteArcs` removes self-loops before SCC analysis. Thus the later self-loop count of zero is not an independent test of original rule self-implications. This removal preserves reflexive-transitive reachability and does not itself invalidate an antisymmetry argument.

## Dependencies and theorem boundary

The actual runtime read closure contains **eight repository files**: three JavaScript modules, `viz/src/data.ts`, `algebra/blind-test-set.json`, and all three files in `corpus50/lanes`. The last four files are read eagerly by `tables.mjs`; their corpus classifications do not enter this experiment's numerical loops. Their inclusion gives no holdout-validation credit. The directory listing and every file's Git/hash identity are bound in [before.json](before.json).

Five additional files were inspected as context, not executed. `formal/v2/f8.mjs` contains a separate rule-saturation `Cn`; `viz/src/laws.ts:closureOf` is a different, depth-limited display helper that traverses alternatives and omits the seed. Neither is called by `m5`, and neither should silently stand in for the intended closure.

Lean defines intrinsic `ex`, proves `ex_reachCl`, and proves `ex_reachCl_union_ex` under antisymmetry of reflexive-transitive reachability. `ex_oplus` additionally takes closed-input premises. The JavaScript's “maximal” orientation reverses the reachability order; the generic Lean identification already explains this convention. These are generic statements, not an encoding of this particular extraction.

To justify `cor:ourconvex` for every subset, select the exact vocabulary/table, encode its relation, prove the intended executable closure agrees with `reachCl` for every input, and establish antisymmetry for that encoded relation. Then instantiate the existing extreme-point and composition results with the same representation. A structural correspondence proof suffices; exhaustive `2^58` execution is unnecessary. Algebraic equality remains separate from the paper's word-RAM complexity proposition.

## Historical comparison and preservation

The fresh seed, split, anti-exchange, composition and principal-closure counts match the frozen historical report text. Its graph summaries print **13/16 arcs**, whereas this run prints **12/15 distinct edges** after deduplication. The paper's 15-arc figure corresponds to the raw-table distinct count, not the LSTAR graph. Old executions retain their original identities; matching counters do not reconstruct their source revision or validate an all-input conclusion.

[The audit JSON](audit.json) contains 20 exact source locators and **182 passing counter/provenance checks**. All **116 protected files**, including all **88 frozen Sprint 10 inputs**, remained unchanged. Full snapshots of runtime inputs and comparison context are retained.

Reviewer: nonauthor GPT-6 through the stock Codex harness; provider telemetry unavailable. No Lean build, new model, native review, original generator modification, corpus change or commit occurred. The resolved standalone Node binary resides under an existing `.foreman/tools` directory; no Foreman orchestrator was invoked. This is a source/measurement audit, not formal correspondence or paper acceptance.

This previously called T.gammaOpen, which\n// reads the reduced 11-row LSTAR; the two disagree on 387 of the 30,856\n// three-element subsets, so the structural measurements below and the\n// constructions in construct.mjs were computing in different models.\n// Semantics are construct.mjs's, including the !external filter.\nexport const openReq = X => T.PARSED_NEW.flatMap(l =>\n  !l.subjects.some(s => X.has(s)) ? A stale DEFIFORMAL_ROOT would\n// silently compute them from another tree, so the override announces itself.\nif (ROOT !== SELF_ROOT) console.error(`tables.mjs: NOTE - reading ${ROOT} (DEFIFORMAL_ROOT), not ${SELF_ROOT}`);\nconst src = fs.readFileSync(`${ROOT}/viz/src/data.ts`, \"utf8\");\n\n// ---------- elements\nexport const ELEMS = {};\nconst RE = /\\{\\s*id:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\",\\s*sym:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\",\\s*name:\\s*\"([^\"]*)\",\\s*group:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\",\\s*stratum:\\s*(\\d),\\s*atom:\\s*\"([NRI])\",\\s*status:\\s*\"([a-z]+)\"/g;\nlet m;\nwhile ((m = RE.exec(src))) {\n  const [, id, sym, name, group, stratum, atom, status] = m;\n  ELEMS[sym] = { id, sym, name, group, stratum: +stratum, atom, status };\n}\nexport const SYMS = new Set(Object.keys(ELEMS));\nexport const MECH = Object.values(ELEMS).filter(e => e.status !== \"limit\").map(e => e.sym);\n\n// ---------- laws\nexport const LAWS = [];\nfor (const l of src.matchAll(/\\{\\s*id:\\s*\"(L\\d+)\",\\s*rule:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"/g)) LAWS.push({ id: l[1], rule: l[2] });\n"},{"id":"parser","original_path":"formal/v2/tables.mjs","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/formal/v2/tables.mjs","sha256":"2d1c5873f562521f12ba07f10bf4b7a7eeafcf76fbc9e0f7afefa8e33dae557e","bytes":9786},"start_line":37,"end_line":58,"byte_start":1857,"byte_end_exclusive":2880,"excerpt_sha256":"061f29a205ea5f59061cc435f18affb812a9e6cf4437bba6a61f985f506925f6","excerpt":"// ---------- THE PARSER. Two variants, so the fix is measurable.\nfunction parseSide(side, corrected) {\n  return side.split(\"+\").map(chunk => {\n    const raw = chunk.trim();\n    const parts = raw.split(\"|\").map(bare);\n    const alts = parts.filter(a => SYMS.has(a));\n    const mixed = alts.length > 0 && alts.length < parts.length;\n    // OLD: external <=> no element alternative at all (a mixed term hard-required its element)\n    // NEW: external <=> no element alternative, OR a prose alternative sits beside one\n    const external = corrected ? (alts.length === 0 || mixed) : (alts.length === 0);\n    return { alts, prose: raw, external, mixed };\n  });\n}\nfunction parseLaws(corrected) {\n  return LAWS.map(l => {\n    const [lhs, rhs = \"\"] = l.rule.split(\"→\");\n    const subjects = (lhs || \"\").split(\"|\").map(bare).filter(s => SYMS.has(s));\n    return { id: l.id, rule: l.rule, subjects, terms: parseSide(rhs, corrected) };\n The **anti-exchange** axiom for a closure operator on `Finset E`: from a closed set `A`\nand two distinct outside points `x`, `y`, at most one of them can be dragged in by adjoining\nthe other. -/\ndef AntiExchange (c : ClosureOperator (Finset E)) : Prop :=\n  ∀ A : Finset E, c A = A → ∀ x y : E, x ∉ A → y ∉ A → x ≠ y →\n    x ∈ c (insert y A) → y ∉ c (insert x A)\n\n/-- The **extreme points** of `A`: those `a ∈ A` not recoverable from the rest of `A`. -/\ndef ex (c : ClosureOperator (Finset E)) (A : Finset E) : Finset E :=\n  A.filter (fun a => a ∉ c (A.erase a))\n\n"},{"id":"generic-reachSet","original_path":"lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","sha256":"3b301a6b0179c36b9936c923805a37938a0127f17121a4140929c980819fbca4","bytes":26100},"start_line":195,"end_line":207,"byte_start":8795,"byte_end_exclusive":9296,"excerpt_sha256":"13e1d95f228f81e8d3267b611d9c7b84ab930e418c4d9edd099bee3e542038cc","excerpt":"/-! ## The reachability part: Theorem R -/\n\nsection Reach\n\nvariable (r : E → E → Prop) [DecidableRel (Relation.ReflTransGen r)]\n\n/-- The set of vertices reachable from `S` along `r`. -/\ndef reachSet (S : Finset E) : Finset E :=\n  Finset.univ.filter (fun x => ∃ s ∈ S, Relation.ReflTransGen r s x)\n\n@[simp] lemma mem_reachSet {S : Finset E} {x : E} :\n    x ∈ reachSet r S ↔ ∃ s ∈ S, Relation.ReflTransGen r s x := by\n  simp only [reachSet, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]\n"},{"id":"generic-anti-exchange-and-ex-identification","original_path":"lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","sha256":"3b301a6b0179c36b9936c923805a37938a0127f17121a4140929c980819fbca4","bytes":26100},"start_line":301,"end_line":327,"byte_start":13096,"byte_end_exclusive":14410,"excerpt_sha256":"6845dcdc2d9d5659d9596db0b1ca5faa9a1abc137bb2cee35784fc22f07be0fd","excerpt":"/-- **Theorem R.** The reachability closure satisfies anti-exchange if and only if the\nreachability preorder is antisymmetric. -/\ntheorem reachCl_antiExchange_iff :\n    AntiExchange (reachCl r) ↔\n      ∀ x y : E, Relation.ReflTransGen r x y → Relation.ReflTransGen r y x → x = y :=\n  ⟨antisymm_of_reachCl_antiExchange r, reachCl_antiExchange_of_antisymm r⟩\n\n/-! ### The extreme points of a reachability closure are the minimal elements -/\n\n/-- For the reachability closure, `ex` computes the `≤`-**minimal** elements of `A`, where\n`≤` is the reachability preorder. (Antisymmetry is not needed for this identification; under\nantisymmetry `≤` is a genuine partial order and these are minimal in the usual sense.) -/\ntheorem ex_reachCl (A : Finset E) :\n    ex (reachCl r) A =\n      A.filter (fun a => ∀ b ∈ A, Relation.ReflTransGen r b a → b = a) := by\n  ext a\n  rw [mem_ex, Finset.mem_filter, reachCl_apply]\n  constructor\n  · rintro ⟨haA, h⟩\n    refine ⟨haA, fun b hbA hba => ?_⟩\n    by_contra hne\n    exact h ((mem_reachSet r).mpr ⟨b, Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hne, hbA⟩, hba⟩)\n  · rintro ⟨haA, h⟩\n    refine ⟨haA, fun hmem => ?_⟩\n    obtain ⟨b, hb, hba⟩ := (mem_reachSet r).mp hmem\n    obtain ⟨hbne, hbA⟩ := Finset.mem_erase.mp hb\n    exact hbne (h b hbA hba)\n"},{"id":"generic-composition-premises","original_path":"lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/lean/Defialgebra/ConvexGeometry.lean","sha256":"3b301a6b0179c36b9936c923805a37938a0127f17121a4140929c980819fbca4","bytes":26100},"start_line":502,"end_line":558,"byte_start":22460,"byte_end_exclusive":25489,"excerpt_sha256":"21000be6653213aff98acbc4eb6536aa405f2080e7f945126566f0d13ec0554a","excerpt":"/-- **Paper `thm:excomp`.** The extreme points of a union are the `≼`-maximal elements of the\nunion of the extreme points — the filter now ranges over the *generators only*, which is what\nmakes the law computable in `|ex A| + |ex B|`. Acyclicity is required. -/\ntheorem ex_reachCl_union_ex\n    (hanti : ∀ x y : E, Relation.ReflTransGen r x y → Relation.ReflTransGen r y x → x = y)\n    (A B : Finset E) :\n    ex (reachCl r) (A ∪ B)\n      = (ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B).filter\n          (fun a => ∀ b ∈ ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B,\n            Relation.ReflTransGen r b a → b = a) := by\n  have hPsub : ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B ⊆ A ∪ B :=\n    Finset.union_subset_union (ex_subset _ A) (ex_subset _ B)\n  ext a\n  rw [ex_reachCl, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]\n  constructor\n  · -- easy direction: minimal over `A ∪ B` implies extreme in its own side and minimal over\n    -- the smaller set of generators\n    rintro ⟨haAB, hmin⟩\n    refine ⟨?_, fun b hb hba => hmin b (hPsub hb) hba⟩\n    rw [Finset.mem_union] at haAB ⊢\n    rcases haAB with h | h\n    · refine Or.inl ?_\n      rw [ex_reachCl, Finset.mem_filter]\n      exact ⟨h, fun b hb hba => hmin b (Finset.mem_union_left _ hb) hba⟩\n    · refine Or.inr ?_\n      rw [ex_reachCl, Finset.mem_filter]\n      exact ⟨h, fun b hb hba => hmin b (Finset.mem_union_right _ hb) hba⟩\n  · -- hard direction: descend an arbitrary `b ≼ a` to an extreme point of its own side\n    rintro ⟨haP, hmin⟩\n    refine ⟨hPsub haP, fun b hb hba => ?_⟩\n    by_contra hne\n    have hdesc : ∃ b' ∈ ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B,\n        Relation.ReflTransGen r b' b := by\n      rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hb with h | h\n      · obtain ⟨b', hb', hb'b⟩ := exists_ex_reach r hanti h\n        exact ⟨b', Finset.mem_union_left _ hb', hb'b⟩\n      · obtain ⟨b', hb', hb'b⟩ := exists_ex_reach r hanti h\n        exact ⟨b', Finset.mem_union_right _ hb', hb'b⟩\n    obtain ⟨b', hb'P, hb'b⟩ := hdesc\n    -- `b'` is a generator reaching `a`, so minimality of `a` over the generators forces\n    -- `b' = a`; then `a` and `b` reach each other and antisymmetry kills the assumption.\n    have hb'a : Relation.ReflTransGen r b' a := hb'b.trans hba\n    have : b' = a := hmin b' hb'P hb'a\n    subst this\n    exact hne (hanti b' b hb'b hba).symm\n\n/-- **Paper `thm:excomp`, in `⊕` form.** For *closed* `A` and `B` the composite is\n`Cn (A ∪ B)` and its canonical form is computed from the canonical forms of the parts. -/\ntheorem ex_oplus\n    (hanti : ∀ x y : E, Relation.ReflTransGen r x y → Relation.ReflTransGen r y x → x = y)\n    {A B : Finset E} (hA : reachCl r A = A) (hB : reachCl r B = B) :\n    ex (reachCl r) (reachCl r (A ∪ B))\n      = (ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B).filter\n          (fun a => ∀ b ∈ ex (reachCl r) A ∪ ex (reachCl r) B,\n            Relation.ReflTransGen r b a → b = a) := by\n  rw [reachCl_union_of_closed r hA hB]\n  exact ex_reachCl_union_ex r hanti A B\n"},{"id":"concrete-corollary","original_path":"paper/atlas.tex","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/paper/atlas.tex","sha256":"a424721a161cba011b682cecc582fa8cc4550a06ba3f2b8a1d3dd7543fdcb704","bytes":152658},"start_line":952,"end_line":960,"byte_start":49335,"byte_end_exclusive":49677,"excerpt_sha256":"79fc7aa3bc02599b811ebce8471efb36aba137fd78fca62e1cd749d90ab235a8","excerpt":"\\begin{corollary}\\label{cor:ourconvex}\n$(\\El, Cn)$ is a convex geometry, on all $2^{58}$ subsets.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\n$D$ has $15$ arcs and $58$ strongly connected components, none non-trivial, so it\nis acyclic; and $Cn$ coincides with reachability in $D$ (checked on $21{,}712$\nseeds). Apply Theorem~\\ref{thm:convex}.\n\\end{proof}\n"},{"id":"composition-and-cost","original_path":"paper/atlas.tex","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/paper/atlas.tex","sha256":"a424721a161cba011b682cecc582fa8cc4550a06ba3f2b8a1d3dd7543fdcb704","bytes":152658},"start_line":966,"end_line":994,"byte_start":49871,"byte_end_exclusive":51220,"excerpt_sha256":"5e354a868d862ddac185576ae2c42fd34e2edda241f58c1e1a419141059a2e09","excerpt":"\n\\begin{theorem}[Composition on canonical forms]\\label{thm:excomp}\nAssume $D$ acyclic (Corollary~\\ref{cor:ourconvex}). For $Cn$-closed $A, B$,\n\\[\n  \\mathrm{ex}(A \\oplus B) \\;=\\; \\max\\nolimits_{\\preceq}\\bigl(\\mathrm{ex}(A) \\cup \\mathrm{ex}(B)\\bigr).\n\\]\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nUnion-stability gives $A \\oplus B = Cn(A \\cup B) = A \\cup B$, and acyclicity\n(Corollary~\\ref{cor:ourconvex}) makes $\\preceq$ a partial order, so the down-set\ngenerated by the union is generated by the $\\preceq$-extremal elements of the\nunion of the generators.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{proposition}[Cost]\\label{prop:excost}\nFix the down-set table of $\\preceq$, an $|\\El| \\times |\\El|$ bit matrix\nindependent of the arguments. On a unit-cost random-access machine with words of\nat least $|\\El|$ bits, $\\mathrm{ex}(A \\oplus B)$ is computed from\n$\\mathrm{ex}(A)$ and $\\mathrm{ex}(B)$ in $O(k)$ word operations, where\n$k = |\\mathrm{ex}(A)| + |\\mathrm{ex}(B)|$.\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nLet $U = \\mathrm{ex}(A) \\cup \\mathrm{ex}(B)$, formed as a bitmask in $O(k)$\noperations. Let $S$ be the bitwise disjunction of the strict down-sets of the\nmembers of $U$, one word each, so $O(k)$ operations. An element $a \\in U$ is\n$\\preceq$-maximal in $U$ exactly when $a \\notin S$, since $a \\in S$ holds iff\nsome $b \\in U$ distinct from $a$ has $a$ strictly below it. The answer is\n"},{"id":"historical-run-text","original_path":"formal/v3/VERIFICATION.md","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/formal/v3/VERIFICATION.md","sha256":"a4e9ca6ab5873bdc65a4b5c3bebef12d14e6cb1edd418a757b222d841e8a1b9c","bytes":22788},"start_line":216,"end_line":259,"byte_start":11531,"byte_end_exclusive":14084,"excerpt_sha256":"df52b3db73f5510c12d982b4e701f025e6b8ea5c7926e4f5dfc433869355e3f9","excerpt":"## 9. `cor:ourconvex` — VERIFIED (with one number off)\n\n> \"D has 15 arcs and 58 strongly connected components, none non-trivial, so it is acyclic; arcs 16; SCCs 58; non-trivial SCCs 0; self-loops 0\nACYCLIC: true\nCn == reachability on all 32567 seeds of size <= 3: mismatches 0\nCn(A u B) == Cn(A) u Cn(B) on 30856 split seeds: failures 0\nanti-exchange over 1697 closed sets x 58^2 pairs (5142758 tests): violations 0\nthm:excomp  ex(A u B) == max(ex A u ex B) over 1464616 closed pairs: failures 0\nelements whose principal closure is themselves (Cn({e}) = {e}): 48 / 58\n```\n\n* **Acyclicity: verified**, 58 SCCs, none non-trivial, no self-loops — under *both* extractions.\n* **`Cn` = reachability: verified exhaustively** on all 32,567 seeds of size ≤ 3 (the paper's\n  21,712 is a subset of this), 0 mismatches.\n* **Union-stability verified** (0 / 30,856), which is the `lem:cm` hypothesis of `thm:convex`.\n* **Anti-exchange verified** by direct exhaustive test over 5.1M configurations, independently of\n  the acyclicity route.\n* **\"15 arcs\" is the wrong table.** The paper's own corrected law system `L*` yields **13 arcs\n  (12 distinct)**. 15 distinct arcs is what the *raw* `data.ts` law strings give (`PARSED_NEW`),\n  which additionally contain `Op→Ct`, `Pf→Ex`, `Pf→Li`. Nothing downstream changes — both\n  digraphs are acyclic and give the same verdicts — but the figure cited should say which\n  extraction it refers to.\n* **`cor:ex`'s honesty caveat is if anything understated**: 49 of 58 elements have\n  `Cn({e}) = {e}`, so the canonical form is the identity on 84% of singletons.\n"},{"id":"separate-Cn-not-called","original_path":"formal/v2/f8.mjs","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/formal/v2/f8.mjs","sha256":"7318a103354e5bfe65e03fe49f365a1e1c48970049c67425a4d37621ec2da838","bytes":8052},"start_line":1,"end_line":11,"byte_start":0,"byte_end_exclusive":881,"excerpt_sha256":"322643495f49eab2df9a198f620d1756a7ed9c7baec49510e4ee3fb741d283c6","excerpt":"// F8 - the Approximation Fixpoint Theory gate, and the stratifiability conjecture.\nimport * as T from \"./tables.mjs\";\nconst key = s => [...s].sort().join(\",\");\nconst U = [\"Fl\", \"Xm\", \"Xf\", \"Rl\", \"Of\", \"Bs\", \"Sl\", \"Au\", \"Gs\", \"Uc\", \"Aw\", \"At\", \"Cp\", \"Cl\", \"Pl\", \"Cd\", \"Ix\", \"Sh\", \"Ct\", \"Li\"];\nconst ALL = []; for (let m = 0; m < (1 << U.length); m++) ALL.push(new Set(U.filter((_, i) => m & (1 << i))));\nconst sub = (a, b) => [...a].every(x => b.has(x));\n// Cn over the definite part of L* (single-alternative terms); the disjunctive part is\n// a constraint, not a production, so it is not part of any consequence operator.\nconst Cn = S => { const X = new Set(S); let ch = true;\n  while (ch) { ch = false; for (const [, subs, terms] of T.LSTAR) if (subs.some(s => X.has(s)))\n    for (const t of terms) if (t.length === 1 && !X.has(t[0])) { X.add(t[0]); ch = true; } } return X; };\n"},{"id":"UI-closure-not-called","original_path":"viz/src/laws.ts","snapshot":{"path":"review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/inputs/viz/src/laws.ts","sha256":"cfc5685a2e117a2d5eb820a8c9f0beac67176fd7d6b7fa96f925fcaa14583d13","bytes":9237},"start_line":148,"end_line":170,"byte_start":5904,"byte_end_exclusive":6717,"excerpt_sha256":"f7b3289cb9f8fddc86c4b62c4232b00e710d152ee7db65c7e86af72386978a6f","excerpt":"\n/** Transitive closure of requirements beneath an element — Photogram's shadow. */\nexport function closureOf(sym: string, depth = 6): { reached: Set<string>; forks: string[][] } {\n  const reached = new Set<string>();\n  const forks: string[][] = [];\n  let frontier = [sym];\n  for (let d = 0; d < depth && frontier.length; d++) {\n    const next: string[] = [];\n    for (const cur of frontier) {\n      for (const law of PARSED) {\n        if (!law.subjects.includes(cur)) continue;\n        for (const t of law.terms) {\n          if (t.external) continue;\n          if (t.alts.length > 1) forks.push(t.alts);\n          for (const a of t.alts) {\n            if (!reached.has(a) && a !== sym) { reached.add(a); next.push(a); }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    frontier = next;\n  }\n  return { reached, forks };\n"}],"missing_correspondence":["Choose the exact concrete58-element vocabulary and law-table extraction; # DeFiFormal migration roadmap

Updated 2026-09-07 UTC: Sprints 7–10 are accepted, delivered and archived. Sprint 10 archive delivery is verified at `ec8f163`. Checked arithmetic and corpus tooling are in implementation under accepted planning gates.
Branch: `semantic-kernel-pivot`. Sprint 8 archive delivery: `9501f0a4`.

The remaining objective is conditional preservation of financial properties
under composition, backed by faithful protocol models. Sprints 1–6 delivered the
pilot, trusted operation contracts, provisional corpus reconstruction, typed
execution/capabilities, conditional sequential preservation and disjoint parallel
composition. Checked boxes
record accepted work; unchecked boxes remain open. Neither implies deployed fidelity.

Sources: [approved migration design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-semantic-kernel-design.md),
[original supplied plan](docs/research/2026-09-06-defi-source-plan.md),
[progress ledger](docs/research/semantic-kernel-progress.md), and
[Sprint 4 adjudication](review/semantic-kernel/sprint4/ADJUDICATION.md).
Historical uppercase `ROADMAP.md` files retain their original evidence and scope.
This root roadmap is the current consolidated agenda.

## 1. Sprint 5: typed interfaces and sequential composition

Accepted with limitations: [OpenSpec change](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-typed-interfaces-sequential-composition/proposal.md),
[design](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-typed-interfaces-sequential-composition/design.md),
and [47 implementation tasks](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-06-typed-interfaces-sequential-composition/tasks.md).
Sequential execution retains the successful prefix and stops at the first refusal.
The [adjudication](review/semantic-kernel/sprint5/ADJUDICATION.md),
[scenario coverage](review/semantic-kernel/sprint5/coverage.md), and
[proof inventory](review/semantic-kernel/sprint5/proof-inventory.json) record the
accepted scope: 93 runtime comparisons, 12 detected source mutants, and 70 named
theorems. Both required native Grok/Fable reviews accepted with limitations.
[Delivery verification](review/semantic-kernel/sprint5/delivery.json) records the
source/evidence push at `5fb0929`; the OpenSpec change is archived and its four main
specifications are synchronized.

- [x] Define component interfaces: typed ports, private/shared state, inputs, outputs, assumptions, and guarantees.
- [x] Define initialization, execution traces, and observable success/refusal behavior.
- [x] Implement sequential composition with explicit state and capability propagation.
- [x] Lift accounting, nonnegativity, authority, and locality results from individual transitions to sequences.
- [x] Prove a frame theorem for predicates that depend only on protected state.
- [x] Add composed reference workflows and mutations covering ordering, refusal propagation, unauthorized interference, and revoked capabilities.

The frame theorem concerns ledger predicates with explicit support and disjoint
writes. Component locality is conditional on denied write access; general private
noninterference is not claimed. Initialization and contract results retain explicit
local/boundary premises, and nonnegativity follows from proof-carrying states.

## 2. Sprint 6: disjoint parallel composition

The [OpenSpec plan](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-disjoint-parallel-composition/design.md)
and [48-task checklist](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-disjoint-parallel-composition/tasks.md)
are implemented and independently reviewed. Source candidate: `fae07ca`.
Both native Grok and Fable audits accepted the Lean implementation and final
evidence with limitations. [Adjudication and review identities](review/semantic-kernel/sprint6/implementation/ADJUDICATION.md)
record the exact reviewed inputs. The accepted source/evidence push
`26bb17d` is verified on `semantic-kernel-pivot`; all 17 requirements were
synchronized to four main specs and the approved change was archived.
[Delivery](review/semantic-kernel/sprint6/delivery.json) and
[archive action](review/semantic-kernel/sprint6/archive-action.json) preserve the records.

Acceptance passes 131 runtime comparisons, 388 imported theorem and 419
supplemental axiom checks with zero forbidden dependencies, all 14 Parallel
mutations, all 45 Parallel runner controls, and all seven historical Python
regression suites. The 126 explicit theorems comprise 88 generic results,
35 reference instances and three counterexamples; generated theorem counts
are separate. A clean repository-package rebuild and frozen administrative
compiler controls also pass. [Coverage](review/semantic-kernel/sprint6/coverage.md)
and [proof inventory](review/semantic-kernel/sprint6/proof-inventory.json) record
all 47 scenarios and their precise evidence classes.

- [x] Pass both planning audits on the same candidate.
- [x] Implement conservative concrete compatibility and independent branch execution.
- [x] Prove full executor dependency, exact refusal framing and both actual serial-order correspondences.
- [x] Prove joined accounting, authority, nonnegativity, supported frames and conditional initialized invariants.
- [x] Complete financial fixtures, real mutations, regressions and native Grok/Fable implementation review.
- [x] Deliver the accepted branch and archive the OpenSpec change.

## Sprint 8: atomic synchronization

The [OpenSpec proposal](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-atomic-synchronization/proposal.md),
[design](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-atomic-synchronization/design.md) and
[40 tasks](openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-07-atomic-synchronization/tasks.md) cover four capabilities,
16 requirements and49 scenarios. The [wiki decision record](wiki-llm/sprint-8-atomic-synchronization.md)
explains exact rollback, separate committed observations and receipt-derived typed
transient clearing. Strict plan validation and author consistency checks pass;
independent GPT-6 and native Fable planning reviews pass on `7a73b2d`. The accepted baseline and dependency delivery passed. Revised implementation candidate `a52fb748` passes135 financial comparisons,357 theorem/496 supplemental axiom checks with zero forbidden dependencies,18 compiling production mutants and65 actual CLI controls. The initial audit-report protocol defect is corrected with its failed attempt preserved. All11 legacy suites have verified relevant dependency equivalence to this revision. Both final native Grok and Opus source/evidence reviews accept with limitations at `99e2e2c`; final65 controls are r4 with the corrected log-path harness. All40 tasks and49 scenarios are complete. Source/evidence push `2c038094` and archive push `9501f0a4` are verified.

The user authorized continued execution of all remaining packages while AFK;
[the execution agenda](wiki-llm/autonomous-execution-agenda.md) preserves dependencies,
review gates and stock Codex execution. The harness goal last reported `usageLimited`; work resumed manually under the user’s authorization. Proposed future work is not accepted
merely because it is scheduled.

## Sprint 9: sequential congruence and configuration preservation

Native Grok and Fable5.1 medium accepted source `eec499d6` and its completed
evidence with limitations. [Adjudication](review/semantic-kernel/sprint9/ADJUDICATION.md)
and [evidence](review/semantic-kernel/sprint9/EVIDENCE.md) record148 runtime
comparisons,14 detected mutations,65 CLI controls and109 explicit theorems.
All16 fresh Lean integration commands passed;13 legacy suites retain their
actual c880 execution identity through checked dependency equivalence.
[Source/evidence delivery](review/semantic-kernel/sprint9/delivery.json) is verified at `ec9ed80`;
[archive integrity](review/semantic-kernel/sprint9/archive-integrity.json) verifies all35 tasks and55 scenarios.

The equivalence/extension milestone covers fixed identity types, explicit
configuration agreement and fixed sequential contexts. Regrouping sequential
steps preserves the full cursor; this does not establish arbitrary parallel
regrouping, causal assume-guarantee rules or capability provenance. Those broader
items remain open below.

## Sprint 10: operational interfaces and binding preservation

Native Grok and Fable 5.1 medium accepted source `b165bc58` and its completed
evidence with limitations. The package adds typed region queries, actual receipt
accounting, initialized total/binding preservation and global binding success
laws over the existing sequential/group/binary shared executors.

All 34 tasks, 17 requirements and 57 scenarios are complete. Evidence records
99 runtime labels, 14 compiling query mutations, 65 CLI controls, 18 Lean commands
and 144 explicit theorems; the imported audit has zero forbidden axioms.
The build is incremental, and one catalog label is an intentional alias.
[Sprint 10 evidence](review/semantic-kernel/sprint10/EVIDENCE.md),
[adjudication](review/semantic-kernel/sprint10/ADJUDICATION.md) and
[verified archive delivery](review/semantic-kernel/sprint10/archive-delivery.json)
retain those limits and exact source/reviewer/run identities.

This ports the region/binding portion of the operational metatheory. General
finite participants, tree regrouping, active extension and atomic transfer remain
open; the broad Interface/Nary roadmap item below is not yet complete.

## Remaining composition and metatheory

- [x] Implement disjoint parallel composition.
- [x] Implement shared-state interleaving with explicit interference conditions.
- [x] Implement atomic synchronization, including failure and transient-settlement semantics.
- [ ] Generalize the useful results in `Interface.lean` and `Nary.lean` into the operational model.
- [ ] Prove behavioral associativity: regrouping compatible components preserves behavior.
- [ ] Prove assume-guarantee composition with initialization and causal or inductive premises, not circular assumptions.
- [x] Define observational equivalence and prove conservative extension: unrelated additions preserve existing behavior.
- [ ] Establish capability provenance and component isolation where required, beyond the current trusted-store assumption.

## 3. Claims, liabilities, and asynchronous behavior

- [ ] Implement actual claims with debtor, creditor, asset/payoff, conditions, due time, and status.
- [ ] Implement creation, transfer, modification, discharge, and default.
- [ ] Prove that liabilities cannot disappear without an authorized lifecycle transition.
- [ ] Add repayment semantics; the current debt-erasure regression only rejects an invalid borrowing proposal.
- [ ] Implement message lifecycles, finality conditions, replay protection, timeouts, challenges, and compensation for asynchronous workflows.
- [ ] Represent oracle, custody, legal, sequencing, and finality assumptions explicitly.

## 4. Corpus and provenance

- [ ] Complete organization → product → version → deployment identities for the 75 candidates reconstructed from 72 historical rows.
- [ ] Resolve the 29 annotation disagreements using rules applicable to future cases.
- [ ] Resolve the separate Liquity V1 liquidation source challenge.
- [ ] Complete remaining product splits, pinned source references, dependency relationships, and ambiguity/residue records.
- [ ] Recover or replace unresolved references from the supplied proposal.
- [ ] Establish separate development and untouched-evaluation manifests. The current 75 candidates remain development cases.

## 5. Certificates and verification infrastructure

- [ ] Define a serialized module/transition format with interfaces, assumptions, invariants, observations, and source mappings.
- [ ] Implement a real certificate checker that recomputes judgments rather than accepting supplied labels.
- [ ] Check typing, footprints, authority, accounting, composition compatibility, library proof instantiation, and outstanding assumptions.
- [ ] Establish correspondence between serialized/executable representations and Lean semantics; do the same for any Quint abstraction introduced.
- [ ] Extend audit coverage to explicit package manifests and declared audit roots.
- [ ] Expand mutation coverage beyond Sprint 5’s 12 sequential mutants: effect application, capability allocation, structural catalog checks, and future composition operators.

## 6. Financial libraries still to port

- [ ] Machine arithmetic: widths, overflow, rounding direction, and fees.
- [ ] Uniswap-style concentrated-liquidity arithmetic and tick traversal.
- [ ] Curve-style iterative invariant calculations and failure behavior.
- [ ] Liquity-style ordered redemption.
- [ ] Morpho-style bad-debt realization and loss allocation.
- [ ] Balancer-style shared vault accounting, hooks, and transient settlement.
- [ ] A complete cross-domain financial workflow.
- [ ] Margin, funding, unsettled profit, liquidation, and bankruptcy handling.
- [ ] External conditional claims, including insurance or tokenized off-chain obligations.

## 7. Protocol fidelity and runtime adapters

- [ ] Pin concrete implementations, versions, deployments, and relevant execution environments.
- [ ] Run identical generated sequences against implementations and models; compare successful and refused behavior.
- [ ] Detect characteristic mutations in rounding, fees, ordering, losses, authority, oracles, and delayed settlement.
- [ ] Prove selected concrete implementation-to-model refinements.
- [ ] Add chain/runtime adapters through verified interfaces. Moriarty, Compact, ZKIR, and proof-carrying transaction integration remain later adapter work.

## 8. Evaluation, research claims, and publication

- [ ] Reconcile remaining paper and ledger claims: Q/Σ, four primitives, semantic minimality, Delta terminology, lattice claims, and exhaustive-result scope.
- [ ] Audit the correspondence between general structural theorems and the concrete historical instances.
- [ ] Freeze the kernel before evaluating untouched cases.
- [ ] Audit the proposed twelve evaluation candidates for prior design use; replace contaminated cases where necessary.
- [ ] Evaluate across the planned execution environments.
- [ ] Report schema coverage, behavioral coverage, library reuse, new kernel concepts, external assumptions, and verification effort separately.
- [ ] Rewrite the paper around demonstrated results and their limits.
- [ ] Update the ontology visualization and repository graph after the schema stabilizes.

## 9. Lower-priority review follow-ups

- [ ] Improve malformed-input diagnostics, standalone schema constraints, and package directory inventory checks.
- [ ] Add explicit current-module-exclusion and broader audit-root fixtures.
- [ ] Add a general duplicate-capability-list theorem and an isolated vault-liquidity regression.
- [ ] Extend individual actor/effect/supply comparison mutations in the older contract wrapper.

- [ ] Strengthen mutation projection guards for attributed declarations/macros/notation/deriving and add separated wrong-world oracles; current concrete Sprint 7 sources are accepted with these recorded limits.

## Acceptance process for each implementation sprint

GPT-6 implements through the stock Codex harness. Lean is the mathematical
authority. Use meaningful negative and mutation checks, independent native Grok
and Fable review, saved evidence bound to exact source/tool identities, and a
verified branch push. Do not use Foreman. Preserve prior proofs, negative results,
and corpus source identities. Keep proofs, bounded execution, measurements,
refutations, and unchecked assumptions distinct.

Current reviewer policy (2026-09-07): the user restored native Fable5.1 at medium
effort. OpenSpec gates use nonauthor GPT-6 plus Fable; implementation/evidence
gates use Grok plus Fable. Completed Opus and historical Fable reports retain
their original model identities. See [working instructions](AGENTS.md).

export const ATLAS_VERSION = "v1.0";

/** Laws naming an element, computed from the law text. */
export function lawsFor(sym: string): Law[] {
  const re = new RegExp(`\\b${sym}\\b`);
  return LAWS.filter((l) => re.test(l.rule));
}

/** Hazard rules naming an element. Membership only — never a magnitude. */
export function hazardsFor(sym: string): Hazard[] {
  const re = new RegExp(`\\b${sym}\\b`);
  return HAZARDS.filter((h) => re.test(h.combo));
}

export interface Law { id: string; rule: string; async: "yes" | "no"; isNew?: boolean }

Source SHA256 cfc5685a2e117a2d5eb820a8c9f0beac67176fd7d6b7fa96f925fcaa14583d13
Rendered SHA256 cfc5685a2e117a2d5eb820a8c9f0beac67176fd7d6b7fa96f925fcaa14583d13

/* The law engine.
 *
 * The 29 laws have been decorative strings until now. They are actually a
 * constraint system: each law fires when one of its subjects is present, and
 * then demands a conjunction of terms, each of which may be a disjunction of
 * element symbols. Parsing them turns the atlas from a picture into something
 * that can pass or fail.
 *
 * Everything downstream needs this — closure for the shadow, seating order for
 * the lock-up, the shape of what is missing when a composition pies.
 */
import { ELEMENTS, HAZARDS, LAWS, type Element } from "./data";

const SYMS = new Set(ELEMENTS.map((e) => e.sym));

/** One requirement term: a disjunction of symbols, or an unresolvable clause. */
export interface Term {
  alts: string[];      // element symbols that would satisfy it
  prose: string;       // the raw text, for terms with no element (e.g. "exit-liquidity")
  external: boolean;   // true when membership alone cannot decide the term
  mixed: boolean;      // an element alternative sits beside a prose one
}

export interface ParsedLaw {
  id: string;
  rule: string;
  subjects: string[];  // symbols that trigger the law; empty = prose subject
  subjectProse: string;
  terms: Term[];
}

/** strip isotope braces and annotations: At{subject=x} -> At */
const bare = (s: string) => s.replace(/\{[^}]*\}/g, "").replace(/[()]/g, "").trim();

function parseSide(side: string): Term[] {
  // split on + at top level; the laws never nest parentheses
  return side.split("+").map((chunk) => {
    const raw = chunk.trim();
    const parts = raw.split("|").map((a) => bare(a));
    const alts = parts.filter((a) => SYMS.has(a));
    // A term like "Tg | bounded emergency process" is a DISJUNCTION. An earlier
    // version dropped the prose alternative and hard-required Tg, which turned
    // five permissive terms into mandatory ones and made L15 alone reject 25 of
    // 72 live protocols. If any alternative is prose we cannot decide the term
    // from membership, so it becomes residue - exactly as a fully-prose term does.
    const mixed = alts.length > 0 && alts.length < parts.length;
    return { alts, prose: raw, external: alts.length === 0 || mixed, mixed };
  });
}

export const PARSED: ParsedLaw[] = LAWS.map((l) => {
  const [lhs, rhs = ""] = l.rule.split("→");
  const subjects = (lhs || "")
    .split("|")
    .map((s) => bare(s))
    .filter((s) => SYMS.has(s));
  return {
    id: l.id,
    rule: l.rule,
    subjects,
    subjectProse: (lhs || "").trim(),
    terms: parseSide(rhs),
  };
});

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ evaluation */

export interface TermResult extends Term { satisfied: boolean; by: string | null }
export interface LawResult {
  law: ParsedLaw;
  firedBy: string[];            // which present symbols triggered it
  terms: TermResult[];
  satisfied: boolean;           // all non-external terms met
  missing: TermResult[];
}

/** Evaluate every law against a set of element symbols. */
export function evaluate(present: string[]): LawResult[] {
  const S = new Set(present);
  const out: LawResult[] = [];
  for (const law of PARSED) {
    const firedBy = law.subjects.filter((s) => S.has(s));
    if (!firedBy.length) continue;
    const terms: TermResult[] = law.terms.map((t) => {
      const by = t.alts.find((a) => S.has(a)) ?? null;
      // an external term cannot be judged from the element set, so it never
      // fails the composition - it becomes residue instead
      return { ...t, satisfied: t.external ? true : !!by, by };
    });
    const missing = terms.filter((t) => !t.satisfied);
    out.push({ law, firedBy, terms, satisfied: missing.length === 0, missing });
  }
  return out;
}

/** Does this set close under the laws it triggers? */
export function closes(present: string[]) {
  const res = evaluate(present);
  const open = res.filter((r) => !r.satisfied);
  return { ok: open.length === 0, results: res, open };
}

/** Hazard rules whose named elements are all present — the joint that will not close.
 *
 *  Polarity matters and an earlier version of this got it backwards. Some rules
 *  describe an element being ABSENT ("Uc with no Aw, At, collateral or
 *  reputation"; "bridged into a representation with no destination-side Aw").
 *  For those, "all named elements present" inverts the meaning. Rules whose text
 *  negates are skipped rather than guessed at — a hazard we cannot evaluate from
 *  membership is residue, not a clean bill of health.
 */
const NEGATED = /\b(no|without|absent|lacking|missing|never)\b/i;

export interface ArmedHazard { id: string; combo: string; cls: string; evaluable: boolean }

export function armedHazards(present: string[]): ArmedHazard[] {
  const S = new Set(present);
  const out: ArmedHazard[] = [];
  for (const h of HAZARDS) {
    const named = [...new Set(
      (h.combo.match(/\b[A-Z][a-z]{1,2}\b/g) || []).filter((m) => SYMS.has(m))
    )];
    if (named.length < 2) continue;                 // not evaluable from membership
    if (NEGATED.test(h.combo)) continue;            // polarity is inverted; skip
    if (named.every((m) => S.has(m))) {
      out.push({ id: h.id, combo: h.combo, cls: h.cls, evaluable: true });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** Hazard rules that membership alone cannot decide — reported, never hidden. */
export function inevaluableHazards(): string[] {
  return HAZARDS.filter((h) => {
    const named = [...new Set(
      (h.combo.match(/\b[A-Z][a-z]{1,2}\b/g) || []).filter((m) => SYMS.has(m))
    )];
    return named.length < 2 || NEGATED.test(h.combo);
  }).map((h) => h.id);
}

/** Laws whose subject is prose, so they can never fire from element membership. */
export function unfireableLaws(): string[] {
  return PARSED.filter((l) => l.subjects.length === 0).map((l) => l.id);
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- closure */

/** Transitive closure of requirements beneath an element — Photogram's shadow. */
export function closureOf(sym: string, depth = 6): { reached: Set<string>; forks: string[][] } {
  const reached = new Set<string>();
  const forks: string[][] = [];
  let frontier = [sym];
  for (let d = 0; d < depth && frontier.length; d++) {
    const next: string[] = [];
    for (const cur of frontier) {
      for (const law of PARSED) {
        if (!law.subjects.includes(cur)) continue;
        for (const t of law.terms) {
          if (t.external) continue;
          if (t.alts.length > 1) forks.push(t.alts);
          for (const a of t.alts) {
            if (!reached.has(a) && a !== sym) { reached.add(a); next.push(a); }
          }
        }
      }
    }
    frontier = next;
  }
  return { reached, forks };
}

/** How many laws require this element — Weight's in-degree. */
export function inDegree(sym: string): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (const law of PARSED) {
    for (const t of law.terms) if (t.alts.includes(sym)) { n++; break; }
  }
  return n;
}

export const IN_DEGREE: Record<string, number> = Object.fromEntries(
  ELEMENTS.map((e) => [e.sym, inDegree(e.sym)])
);

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ seating order */

/** The order the joints close in: a required element seats before the element
 *  that requires it, regardless of the causal order it was composed in. */
export function seatingOrder(present: string[]): string[] {
  const S = new Set(present);
  const need = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const sym of present) need.set(sym, new Set());
  for (const law of PARSED) {
    for (const subj of law.subjects) {
      if (!S.has(subj)) continue;
      for (const t of law.terms) {
        const hit = t.alts.find((a) => S.has(a));
        if (hit && hit !== subj) need.get(subj)!.add(hit);
      }
    }
  }
  const out: string[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const visit = (s: string, guard: Set<string>) => {
    if (seen.has(s) || guard.has(s)) return;   // guard breaks reflexive cycles
    guard.add(s);
    for (const dep of need.get(s) ?? []) visit(dep, guard);
    guard.delete(s);
    seen.add(s);
    out.push(s);
  };
  for (const s of present) visit(s, new Set());
  return out;
}

/** Elements that sit in a requirement cycle — the reflexive bind. */
export function cycles(present: string[]): string[][] {
  const S = new Set(present);
  const edges = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const law of PARSED) {
    for (const subj of law.subjects) {
      if (!S.has(subj)) continue;
      const outs: string[] = [];
      for (const t of law.terms) {
        const hit = t.alts.find((a) => S.has(a));
        if (hit) outs.push(hit);
      }
      edges.set(subj, [...(edges.get(subj) ?? []), ...outs]);
    }
  }
  const found: string[][] = [];
  const stack: string[] = [];
  const state = new Map<string, number>();
  const dfs = (n: string) => {
    state.set(n, 1); stack.push(n);
    for (const m of edges.get(n) ?? []) {
      if (state.get(m) === 1) found.push(stack.slice(stack.indexOf(m)));
      else if (!state.get(m)) dfs(m);
    }
    stack.pop(); state.set(n, 2);
  };
  for (const s of present) if (!state.get(s)) dfs(s);
  return found;
}

export function symsOf(list: Element[]) { return list.map((e) => e.sym); }

# Historical claim reconciliation author draft

The [OpenSpec author draft](../openspec/changes/historical-claim-reconciliation/proposal.md)
proposes four capabilities,18 requirements,45 scenarios and27 unchecked tasks.
It has not passed the nonauthor GPT-6/native Fable planning gate and contains no
implementation or newly verified mathematical result.

It starts from the delivered [18 claim-site findings](../review/semantic-kernel/claim-reconciliation/preparation-r2/REPORT.md)
and the [actual historical-instance audit](../review/semantic-kernel/historical-instance-audit/REPORT.md).
The former binds63 excerpts from22 files; the latter records the unchanged m5
run at4d42600 with its real nonempty counters. These records retain their original
identities; this draft does not rerun them.

The proposed work has three independently reviewable deliverables: source-specific
claim dispositions and selected prose corrections; a universal Lean bridge for
the exact LSTAR and PARSED_NEW unary graphs; and a wrapper that evaluates actual
bounded counters rather than trusting exit0. Final acceptance joins the evidence
without promoting measurements into proofs. All historical theorem statements,
proofs, generators, corpus inputs and prior reports remain unchanged.

The Lean bridge uses a literal58-symbol encoding and an independently defined
finite saturation executor. It proves equality to reachability for every input,
checks concrete antisymmetry, then instantiates the existing intrinsic extreme-point
and composition results. Fixed-source extraction and reviewed JavaScript algorithm
translation remain explicit trust boundaries; no verified V8/parser claim follows.
A full-instance statement outside the encoded unary fragment remains open if its
exact closure cannot be bound.

The correction policy preserves valid stronger arguments. A fully admissible pair
whose union contains a purely negative forbidden set has no admissible common
upper bound. Loss of union closure alone does not prove that result, and a
repairable mixed clause is insufficient. Wide CNF clauses likewise provide only
syntactic evidence unless a full-instance majority counterexample or proof exists.
The default bounded correction withdraws unsupported inferences without pretending
to refute stronger conclusions that might have another proof.

S9 operational sequential composition is accepted. S10 interfaces, M3 finite
participants and M4 operational regrouping remain separate pending packages.
Corpus adjudication owns source/identity judgments; all12 proposed evaluation
cases remain development-exposed and untouched evaluation stays blocked pending
its own freeze and selection. Full paper rewriting, complexity, deployments and
runtime adapters are outside this change.

The draft's author also authored historical audit and corpus research evidence;
an independent planning reviewer must not count this author as a nonauthor.
The current policy requires GPT-6 stock-harness implementation, same-candidate
nonauthor GPT-6 plus native Fable5.1 medium planning review, and native Grok plus
Fable result review. No Foreman or native review was invoked for this draft.
